description.narrative: The project is proposed by Oxfam, in partnership with ESDC, in response to the escalating food security crisis in the Gaza Strip, exacerbated by the ongoing conflict and protracted humanitarian situation. Decades of restrictions and recent escalations have decimated the agricultural sector, leaving vulnerable HHs and smallholder farmers in a precarious state, heavily reliant on external aid.directly addresses these critical needs by focusing on the restoration of agricultural livelihoods as a pathway to enhanced food security and resilience. The project will benefit 1193 individuals belonging to 213 vulnerable HHs and small-scale farmers in Gaza City, North Gaza, the Middle Area, and Khan Yunis. The project’s core strategy is to provide comprehensive agricultural support across three key intervention areas. Firstly, it will reactivate local agriculture service providers by supporting with inputs, two strategically located plant nurseries in Gaza City and North Gaza, and benefiting a total of 100 HHs. These nurseries are vital for the agricultural input supply chain, providing essential seedlings and technical advice to farmers. The project will provide conditional cash-based transfers to selected nurseries, enabling them to repair damaged infrastructure, procure necessary equipment, and resume operations, ensuring a sustainable supply of quality inputs for the wider agricultural community. Secondly, the project will scale up urban and peri-urban home gardening initiatives, directly empowering 80 vulnerable households in Gaza City and the Middle Area. Recognizing the potential of urban agriculture to enhance household food security and dietary diversity, the project will provide comprehensive home gardening support packages. Technical support and training will be provided to participating households to ensure the successful establishment and maintenance of productive home gardens, fostering a sustainable source of fresh produce at the householdlevel. Thirdly, the project will support 33 small farming HHs in South Gaza (Beni Suhila area, Khan Yunis) to rehabilitate their agricultural livelihoods and restore their productive capacities for seasonal farming. Targeting 50 dunums of agricultural land, the project will provide support package to selected smallholder farmers including leveling, plowing, and mulching, facilitated through aservice provider and with fuel provision. Additionally, farmers will receive essential agricultural inputs such as irrigation networks and fertilizers, enabling them to resume cultivation and contribute to local food production. The expected impact of this project is multifaceted. For vulnerable households, it will directly enhance their access to fresh and nutritious food, improving dietary diversity and reducing reliance on increasingly scarce and costly market supplies. Home gardening initiatives will empower households, particularly women, with skills and resources to contribute to their own food security. For smallholder farmers, the project willenable the rehabilitation of productive land and the resumption of seasonal farming activities, restoring their livelihoods and contributing to the local economy. By reactivating nurseries, the project will strengthen the entire agricultural input supply system, benefiting a wider range of farmers beyond the direct beneficiaries.

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam Novib has been active in the Occupied Palestinian Territory/Israel (OPT/I) since 1982 and working with Palestinian refugees in Lebanon since the mid 1980s. It has built up a strong network of relationships with local NGOs and counts among its localcounterparts some of the largest and most professional NGOs in various sectors. It has accompanied these NGOs in their development from ad hoc volunteer groups to sizeable professional institutions with national outreach. At the same time the conceptualisation of the programme has evolved from three country programs in the early 1990s to a program for Palestinians in the Middle East (PME) working withPalestinians in OPT, Israel and Lebanon.
The programme has changed over the years with the establishment of the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the mid-1990s from a focus on support and service provision at a grassroots level and grassroots mobilization, to working towards influencing the establishment of the PA, its lawmaking and supporting building a democratic state # this involved supporting efforts of Palestinian civil society to build the basis for a democratic Palestinian state with room for civil participation, ensuring inclusion of vulnerable groups, refugees and women, and shaping its laws and systems. Oxfam Novib has also supported partners that are working on the provision of humanitarian assistance, response preparedness and conflict transformation. We have also supported partners in the provision of health services, access to quality education and gender justice.
